script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Psychological
Theme: friendship

Begin screenplay.

---

FADE IN:

EXT. NIGHT - A CITY PARK

A lone figure, JAMES (40s, a distressed but thoughtful man) paces restlessly through the dimly lit park.

JAMES
(whispering to himself)
I can't do this alone. I can't...

Suddenly, he hears a rustling in the bushes behind him. He turns to face a young woman, LUCY (early 30s, warm and approachable), sitting on a nearby bench.

LUCY
(smiling)
Looks like you could use some company.

INT. JAMES' APARTMENT - DAY

James and Lucy sit at the kitchen table, surrounded by empty takeout boxes.

LUCY
(eating a sandwich)
You know, James, you seem like a really smart guy. Why don't you reach out to someone for help instead of going through this alone?

JAMES
(sighs)
It's not that simple. I've burned every bridge I've ever had. My family... my friends... they're all gone.

Lucy looks at him sympathetically.

LUCY
Well, I'm here now. I believe in you, James. I really do.

EXT. JAMES' OFFICE - DAY

James stands before a group of colleagues, each staring at him with disdain. He feels a heavy weight in his chest as they dismiss his ideas.

LUCY (V.O.)
(from off-screen)
You've got this, James. Don't give up.

INT. JAMES' APARTMENT - NIGHT

James sits at the kitchen table, staring at a blank computer screen. He's overwhelmed with self-doubt.

Suddenly, the doorbell rings. It's Lucy, bearing a tray of hot chocolate and a stack of papers.

LUCY
I thought you could use a break. You've been working nonstop lately.

JAMES
(touched)
Lucy, thank you. This means more to me than you know.

INT. ART GALLERY - DAY

James and Lucy stroll through the gallery, admiring the artwork. A painting catches James' eye – a self-portrait of a woman with a determined expression.

JAMES
(pointing to the painting)
This is beautiful. She looks like she's ready to conquer the world.

LUCY
(smiling)
Sometimes, all it takes is believing in yourself and having someone there to support you.

INT. JAMES' APARTMENT - NIGHT

James sits at the kitchen table, working late into the night. Lucy enters the room, carrying a steaming cup of tea.

LUCY
You're pushing yourself too hard. Get some rest.

James looks up, surprised.

JAMES
I didn't realize how much I needed this.

They share a quiet moment, sipping their tea in the dimly lit room.

EXT. PARK - DAY

James and Lucy sit on a bench in the park, surrounded by blossoming cherry trees.

LUCY
You know, James, I believe in you. And I think you'll find that there are still people who believe in you, too.

JAMES
(teary-eyed)
Thank you, Lucy. I don't know what I'd do without you.

They share a warm, heartfelt hug.

FADE OUT.

---

THE END
